findings.title: Light-theme lightness value changed from 30% to 70% in embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR changes it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, i.e. the light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70% lightness. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original light-mode value and only adds the dark-theme variant (expected: 30% / 70%). This makes the username link in expanded/embedded posts much lighter than before on light color schemes, reducing contrast and breaking visual consistency with the equivalent common/base/topic-post.scss rule (30%/70%).

findings.title: .custom-message-length lightness values inverted relative to original and desktop
findings.body: The mobile `.custom-message-length` rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme value was changed from 70% to 30%, and the dark value is 70% — the opposite of the pattern used everywhere else in this PR (including desktop/modal.scss, which uses 70%/30% for the same `.custom-message-length` selector). On light color schemes this makes the flag character-count hint far darker than before, and it will now diverge between mobile and desktop.

findings.title: Topic map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50% on mobile
findings.body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. All other 20%→converted rules in this PR use 20%/80% (see the adjacent `.map .number, i` rule in the same file, and desktop/topic-post.scss h3 which uses 20%/80%). The light-theme branch was silently changed from 20% to 50%, making the topic map heading noticeably lighter on mobile light themes and inconsistent with desktop.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value changed from 30% to 50%, which does not match the analogous rule in common/base/user.scss (`.username a` uses 30%/70%) or the dark value that should mirror it (70%). Member names in the group member list will be lighter/lower-contrast than before on light themes.

findings.title: Mobile group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same issue as the desktop counterpart: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50%. The consistent conversion (30%/70%) is used elsewhere (e.g. common/base/user.scss). This silently lightens member names in the mobile group member list on light color schemes.
